W1_BOGOMOLOV_REIDER.reason: The source-complete full genus-defect cluster is on the wrong side of the Bogomolov-instability inequality. A materially smaller canonical cluster would be a new route, not a continuation of this cheap test.

W2_SYMBOLIC_WALDSCHMIDT_EFFECTIVITY.cheap_test: Riemann-Roch effectivity of the exact ray
W2_SYMBOLIC_WALDSCHMIDT_EFFECTIVITY.reason: The exact divisor class D_l is effective for every l>=1, independently of the arrangement of the fourteen exceptional indices. Therefore an effectivity-only symbolic/Waldschmidt threshold cannot exclude the active ray.

W3_AUT_NORM_INVARIANT_SECTION.cheap_test: orbit-averaged norm class and known test curves
W3_AUT_NORM_INVARIANT_SECTION.reason: Symmetry amplification moves the class deeper into a big positive region instead of creating a numerical vanishing overload. A refined representation-theoretic invariant-ring obstruction would be a different theorem.

W4_K3_QUOTIENT_PUSHDOWN.cheap_test: all seven coordinate-sign K3 numerical pushdowns

formula.fixed_supported: f=# supported nodes fixed/contracted by sigma

W4_K3_QUOTIENT_PUSHDOWN.why_survives: The first numerical tests do not contradict the pushdowns, but unlike the parked adapter routes the 2026 K3 quotient supplies a rank-20 Picard lattice generated by explicit curves and 15 elliptic fibrations. A second shallow scan can test the seven pushdown classes directly against that fixed lattice/curve inventory without branch-lift reconstruction.

W6_MODULAR_FORM_VALENCE.cheap_test: boundary-factor valence on the two zero-pairing quartics
W6_MODULAR_FORM_VALENCE.modular_input: box coordinates are invariant products of weight-1/2 theta generators on X(8)xX(8)
W6_MODULAR_FORM_VALENCE.retained_saturation: for each zero quartic the two relevant factor-quotient fibers are already completely reduced and fully occupied; degrees are 28*l in e=2 and 56*l in e=4
W6_MODULAR_FORM_VALENCE.reason: The obvious factorwise valence budget is saturated exactly, not exceeded. A modular-form argument would need a new coupled two-factor relation rather than a pure zero-count/valence inequality.
